Mission enters later. It names a sharper direction that can organize work once a person has already built enough ability and freedom to act on it. The chapter is therefore a doorway into the rest of Rule 4. It does not ask the reader to invent a life purpose overnight. Its job is to prepare the later argument that missions require capital, exploration, and visibility. Rule 4 starts by making meaningful work more disciplined than wishful purpose language. Rule 4 begins by asking a different question from the one that ended Rule 3. Newport answers by opening the mission argument. That shift works because mission is not just passion with a fancier label. Passion was vague and early. Mission is tighter and later. It gives work a real direction once skill and autonomy have created enough room to move. This chapter is the launchpad, not the full build.
